html:
Ndongo was a kingdom of the Kimbundu-speaking Mbundu people in the highlands between the Lukala and Kwanza rivers, in what is now northern Angola. The map shows it in 1492 and 1500, when it was still a tributary of its powerful northern neighbour Kongo. Its kings bore the title ngola, which the Portuguese turned into the name Angola.

Ndongo broke away from Kongo in the 1500s and traded with Portuguese merchants, mostly in slaves. After Portugal founded Luanda in 1576, almost a century of war followed as the Portuguese pushed inland to feed the Atlantic slave trade.

Queen Nzinga led the resistance from the 1620s, at times allied with the Imbangala and the Dutch, and ruled from neighbouring Matamba. Ndongo's last stronghold, Pungo Andongo, fell in 1671, and its land became part of Portuguese Angola.
